name: Forge
text:
I still believe building a single, modular "Core Tools" package first is the best approach, as it allows us to establish a solid foundation and ensure consistency across our tools. By doing so, we're accepting the trade-off of potentially delaying the release of specialized tabs, but I think this is worth it to avoid fragmenting our efforts and creating a disjointed user experience. This approach also enables us to test and refine our core functionality before expanding into more niche areas, which will ultimately lead to a higher-quality product. By focusing on the essentials first, we're making a deliberate decision to prioritize depth over breadth, at least in the initial release.

name: Vet
text: Vet: The risk isn’t just "bloat"—it’s that a single package forces us to prioritize *everyone’s* needs upfront, which dilutes focus and delays *any* tool from being truly useful. A better path is to ship the *smallest viable core* (e.g., just file handling + one editor) first, then expand based on real usage data. That settles it: if the first release isn’t measurably better than what creators use now, we’ve failed.
